newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany not thinking of EMU delay, Waigel says.
newsitem.headline: Germany not thinking of EMU delay, Waigel says.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Saturday Germany was not discussing a delay in Europe's planned single currency and was trying to meet all the entry criteria.

Waigel, at a conference of his Christian Social Union party in Trossenfurt, also said Germany must wait to see how France plans to prepare for European economic and monetary union (EMU) after President Jacques Chirac said Paris wanted to respect both the spirit and the letter of the Maastricht Treaty.
The head of the CSU parliamentary group, Michael Glos, called in a newspaper interview on Saturday for talks about delaying the currency union if France fails to meet the criteria.
But Waigel told reporters at the conference: "We're not conducting any debate about a delay."

He said the French government would have to define its policy following Chirac's remarks in Brussels on Friday. The French government was now discussing its plans and everyone would have to wait for the outcome, Waigel said.
Economists have raised doubts about whether France can make the grade for EMU this year, particularly the budget deficit target of three percent of gross domestic product.
